K_problems.problem: 25 required fields with no partial save
K_problems.why: I'd fill this out on my phone, and 25 fields with no save means one interruption loses everything. That's well over my 15 minutes. I'd quit around field 6.

K_problems.problem: Trade licence no. and Industry code (ISIC) are required
K_problems.why: I'm pre-revenue and might not have a licence yet. I have no idea what ISIC means. Required fields I can't fill mean a dead end.

K_problems.problem: Mission*, Vision*, Scope in*, Scope out*, Preferred methodology*
K_problems.why: This is consultant jargon. I came here because I don't know the methodology. Asking me to pick one is backwards.

K_problems.problem: KPI 1/2 with unit and horizon, plus Risk appetite 1–10
K_problems.why: I don't know what my KPIs should be. That's part of what I'm asking for. Risk appetite on a 1–10 scale means nothing to me, so I'd just guess.
Forcing three makes me invent them. My only real constraint is that I have no money.

K_problems.problem: Data owner and Decision owner emails
K_problems.why: That's me for every one. It feels like the form was built for a big company, not someone like me.

K_problems.problem: Title 'Create Engagement (EngagementSpec)' and 'EvidenceItems for M02 critical gaps'
K_problems.why: These are internal system names. It reads like a developer screen, so I don't trust it was made for me.

K_problems.problem: Data gaps named sales_tx, cust_master, mkt_spend_ts
K_problems.why: I can't tell what files these mean. Is sales_tx my Stripe export? I've never spent on ads, so what do I upload for mkt_spend_ts?

K_problems.problem: Red/green dots with no text label
K_problems.why: I can't tell whether red means missing, wrong or urgent. On a small phone screen the dots are hard to see anyway.
You can't drag files on a phone. On mobile I literally can't upload anything.
I don't have most of this data. The screen assumes I do and gives me no other way forward.

K_problems.problem: 'Error 422: schema mismatch' toast that disappears after 3 seconds
K_problems.why: It's gone before I've read it, I don't know what a schema is, and it doesn't say how to fix the file or show what a correct one looks like.

K_problems.problem: Session expires after 10 minutes of inactivity
K_problems.why: While I go dig the export out of Stripe, the session times out and I lose my place.

K_problems.problem: Status screen with only a spinner
K_problems.why: It doesn't say how long, what's happening, whether I need to do anything, or whether I'll get notified. I'd keep checking it, then give up.

K_problems.problem: No price or cost shown anywhere
K_problems.why: I'm on a low budget, so I'm worried a bill is coming that I don't know about.

walkthrough: 0–2 min: I open the link on my phone and type 'should I raise prices or spend on ads?'. That's easy and it feels normal, like WhatsApp.

2–7 min: It asks one question at a time: what I sell, current price, how many customers, margins. I can answer most of it, but 'what's your gross margin?' makes me stop and guess. A few back-and-forth messages.
7–9 min: The summary card shows the problem, my suspected cause and other possible causes. Seeing other causes I hadn't thought of is useful. I tap [That's right].

9–14 min: Data requests come one message at a time with a reason. I can connect Stripe, which is easy. For 12 months of orders I only have 3, so I'm not sure whether to upload anyway or tap [I don't have this]. For ad spend I have none, so I tap [I don't have this]. I don't know what happens after that. Will the analysis still work?
Session ends. The next day I come back and have to scroll up to find where I was and whether anything is still waiting on me. This is a likely place to drop off.

Days later an email says it's ready. The report is a long chat message. The summary at the top is good on a phone. The expandable sections are fine. I ask a follow-up in the chat, which I really like.
I'm still not sure how confident it is, given it only had 3 months of data.
A.quote: Talking to it was easy, but when I said I don't have ad data, I had no idea if that killed the whole thing. Then I came back two days later and had to scroll to figure out where we were.

walkthrough: 0–4 min: Step 1, company profile, 6 fields. OK, but some don't fit a pre-revenue startup.
4–6 min: Step 2, category. Is pricing vs. ads Sales or Finance? I pick Sales, then describe it.
6–11 min: Step 3, Goals and KPIs. The suggestions help a bit, but I don't really know my KPIs, so I pick 'Revenue growth' and guess the rest. This is the first point I'd consider quitting.
11–14 min: Step 4, constraints and budget. I put a tiny budget and wonder if they'll judge me. Step 5, submit. The draft save is a relief because I run out of time here.

Next session: The data page is a table. On a phone the columns are cramped. There are templates to download, but I can't edit Excel templates well on my phone. There's no 'I don't have this' option, so I leave the ad spend row empty and it shows as incomplete.
Dashboard: 'Data completeness 40%'. Is that bad? Do I need to do something? There's no clear next step. I'd stop checking.
Report: a formal PDF with methodology and a confidence appendix. Way too long to read on my phone. I skim the executive summary. The 'confidence appendix' at the end feels like the fine print.
C.quote: It felt like applying for a bank loan. Then the dashboard said 40% and I had no idea if that was my problem or theirs.

walkthrough: 0–3 min: One text box. I type my question in my own words and maybe attach my spreadsheet. The 3–5 follow-up questions are short. Easy.
3–5 min: The 'Your next step' card says 'Confirm we understood your problem (2 min)'. I read 'What we understood' and the other possible causes. I fix one line with [Edit]. Done.

5–14 min: Next step: 'Upload 2 files'. The data checklist explains in plain words why each item is needed and gives step-by-step 'how to get it from Stripe'. I connect Stripe. The spreadsheet's first upload fails, but it explains what's wrong and shows an example, so I fix it. Ad spend is marked 'Helpful', not 'Must have', and I tap [We don't have it → what happens instead]. Telling me what happens instead is exactly what I needed.
It saves automatically. I close my phone with no stress.
Between sessions: no messages unless I need to act. Then a WhatsApp: results are ready. The card at the top had already told me 'Nothing needed from you. Results expected Thu'.

Report: the answer in one paragraph first. Then steps. Then 'How sure are we?' The pricing finding is Moderate and ads are 'Not yet tested', with what would make it stronger, e.g. 'run a $200 test for 2 weeks'. I tap [Ask a question about this] on one finding.
Small worries: it's a long page on a phone, and the progress tracker has 6 steps when I only care about the next one.
B.quote: For once something told me what to do next and how long it would take. And it actually said 'we're not sure about the ads part because you have no data', and I trust that more than a confident answer.

interrogation.a: Being asked for something I don't have, like a trade licence, KPIs or 12 months of ad data, with no way past it. A required field I can't answer is where I close the tab.
interrogation.b: A plain answer with my own numbers in it (e.g. 'your 3 months of Stripe show X customers at $Y'), an honest note that it's based on only 3 months, and a cheap, small test I can run this month to check it, like raising the price on one product or a $200 ad test. Also a human name saying they checked it.
interrogation.c: In B: make it phone-first by collapsing everything except the 'next step' card and the report answer. Put the price and turnaround up front. Add a short glossary tap on any jargon term. Let me answer the follow-up questions by voice note.
interrogation.d: Since I don't know what data matters, give me a 'founders like you' starter: a 2-minute example report for a similar tiny D2C business, so I can see what I'd get before I commit. And turn the report's recommendation into a tiny experiment plan with a check-in reminder ('in 2 weeks, tell us what happened') so the tool learns from my real result instead of my thin data.
